title: Left restriction is invisible to the symplectic form on the support submodule
statement:
Fix a prime $p$ and a natural number $n$, and let $M \subseteq \{0,1,\dots,n-1\}$ be a set of coordinates. For every $s \in V$ and every $v \in V_M$ (that is, every $v$ supported on $M$),
\[
\omega\bigl(r_M^V(s),\, v\bigr) = \omega(s, v).
\]
In words: applying the restriction endomorphism $r_M^V$, which zeroes out the coordinates outside $M$, to the left argument of the symplectic form leaves the value unchanged whenever the right argument is supported on $M$.
hypotheses_covered: M is a finite set of coordinates in {0,...,n-1}
s is an arbitrary vector in V
v lies in the support submodule V_M (supp(v) ⊆ M)
replaced: If $v \in V_M$, then $\omega(r_M^V(s), v) = \omega(s, v)$ for all $s \in V$.
